standard_prerequisites.name: The notion of a subbase for a topological space, and the definition of quasi-compactness as the finite-refinement property of open coverings
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's sections on quasi-compact spaces and maps, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the hypothesis on the subbase and the conclusion to be proved.

core_obligations: The maximal covering: assuming a covering without a finite refinement exists, the proof applies Zorn's lemma to obtain a maximal such covering, and records the equivalent formulation that adding any open not among its members creates a finite refinement (proof lines 2190-2196).

Reduction to the subbase: the proof restricts attention to the members of the covering that lie in the subbase and shows that they already cover the space, using the maximality of the chosen covering (proof lines 2196-2204).

The finite refinement: by the hypothesis on the subbase this subfamily has a finite refinement; the proof then uses maximality once more to replace each of the finitely many covering members by finitely many members of the original covering (proof lines 2204-2208).
Contradiction: the resulting finite subfamily covers the space, contradicting the choice of the maximal covering, which proves quasi-compactness (proof lines 2208-2210).
proof_roadmap: 反设存在无有限细化的开覆盖，由 Zorn 引理取极大的一个；“加进任何不在其中的开集就产生有限细化”。
只看覆盖中属于子基的成员，由极大性它们已覆盖 X；由题设它们有有限细化，再用极大性把每个成员换成有限多个原覆盖成员，得到原覆盖的有限细化，矛盾。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is Alexander's subbase theorem in the form the chapter uses (author lemma at source lines 2182-2187, label lemma-subbase-theorem, bearing the author's own bracketed name): a subbase whose coverings always have finite refinements forces the space to be quasi-compact. The proof (source lines 2189-2210) is the classical Zorn argument, complete in the author's own presentation: it chooses a maximal covering without a finite refinement (proof lines 2190-2196), shows that the members lying in the subbase already cover the space (proof lines 2196-2204), applies the hypothesis to obtain a finite refinement, and uses maximality a second time to turn that refinement into a finite subcovering of the original covering, giving the contradiction (proof lines 2204-2210). The theorem is the tool by which the chapter verifies quasi-compactness of spectral spaces and of limits. H2.
